C0.quote: Liquid democracy is a voting paradigm that allows voters to choose
C0.note: Liquid democracy: binary votes aggregated by weighted majority after transitive delegation.

C1.quote: satisfies probabilistic do no harm and probabilistic positive gain with respect
C1.note: All main results (Theorems 1-3, via Lemma 1) show that behavioural delegation models keep concentration of power bounded so that the gain in probability of identifying the ground truth relative to direct voting is non-negative/positive; this is performance against an epistemic accuracy objective (WD). The 'properties' are accuracy-performance criteria satisfied by models of voter behaviour, not axioms characterising or classifying aggregation rules, so AX is not coded.

C2.1.value: binary votes Vi (with delegations forming a delegation graph Gn)
C2.1.quote: over the n possible binary votes Vi

C2.2.quote: voters are making a decision on a binary issue
C2.2.note: Input is a binary vote in {0,1} (correct/incorrect alternative), plus each voter's choice to vote directly or delegate to another voter.

C2.3.loc: Section 2 Model, p.5; Appendix A, p.24
C2.3.quote: Each voter i has a competence level pi ∈ [0, 1]
C2.3.note: Competence pi is attributed to voters independently of their vote and is explicitly treated as the voter's type in Appendix A ('we take a voter's type to be their competence'); no preferences or utilities appear.

C2.4.quote: Let Vi = 1 if voter i would vote correctly
C2.4.note: Competence pi and vote Vi ~ Bern(pi) are separate objects with separate notation; the vote is a random draw given competence. Doubt: C2.3 could be read as N (competence is an ability rather than an attitude), which would give ONE.

C3.1.quote: our models do not take strategic considerations into account
C3.1.note: Votes and delegations are stochastic according to fixed models; no strategic misreporting analysed.

C3.2.loc: Checked: Abstract; Section 1 Introduction and 1.1, pp.1-4; Section 2 Model, pp.5-6; Section 7 Discussion, pp.19-20
C3.2.note: The paper states voters are non-strategic and vote correctly with probability pi, but does not state that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.note: C2.2 is OTH only and no utility/welfare/satisfaction/cost/distortion notions for voters are used.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.loc: Section 2 Model, Gain of a delegation instance, p.5
C5.1.quote: the difference between the probability that liquid democracy is correct
C5.1.note: Outcomes are evaluated by epistemic accuracy (probability of selecting the ground truth) and concentration of power, none of the listed welfare/representation criteria.

VOT.quote_behav: our models do not take strategic considerations into account
VOT.note: Voters vote (Vi ~ Bern(pi)) or delegate according to exogenous stochastic delegation models M = (q, phi), described as capturing 'independent voter behavior'. Info is NA because behaviour is non-strategic; the paper notes a voter 'does not need to know' others' competence (Section 1.1, p.2).

CAN.note: Alternatives are a correct and an incorrect option; no candidates act.

ORG.note: Central planners appear only in related work, not in the model.

DES.note: Delegation models are studied as descriptions of voter behaviour, not as a designer's choice.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

C9.2.loc: Section 7 Discussion, pp.19-20; Section 2 Model, pp.5-6
C9.2.quote: our models do not take strategic considerations into account
C9.2.note: Needed assumptions: existence of a ground truth (stated and discussed, p.19), votes independent Bernoulli draws from competence (stated, p.5; independence discussed p.20), voters non-strategic (stated, p.20), delegation behaviour following the (q, phi) models without a restricting social network (stated, Sections 1.1, 2, 7). All are stated as modelling assumptions.

C1.reason: Do-no-harm and positive-gain are accuracy-performance criteria against the ground truth satisfied by behavioural delegation models rather than axiomatic properties of a rule, so WD alone applies (B's codes kept, with a verbatim 11-word quote replacing B's over-long quote about prior work).
